title: Northfield Logistics — Before/After Redwood Optimize savings analysis
summary: Working draft: quantitative before/after analysis for Northfield Logistics (NL) showing estimated monthly spend and unit economics for their mixed workload (chat + retrieval + embeddings). This file compares the current NL deployment (baseline) to a proposal that applies Redwood Optimize recommendations: model quantization + 8-bit runtime, per-route batching policies, hot-prefix KV caching for RAG flows, and split routing to a cheaper 7B variant for non-critical routes.
customer: Northfield Logistics (supply-chain TMS provider) — heavy daytime generation traffic for customer support chat, nightly bulk embeddings for cross-indexing, and occasional long-sequence reranking jobs.
workload_profile: Monthly tokens: 220M generation tokens, 95M embedding tokens. Peak QPS: 42 requests/sec (day), median latency SLO: 250ms for chat route, batchable overnight jobs for embeddings/rerank. Average seq length: chat 180 tokens, retrieval context 1200 tokens for rerank jobs.
baseline_costs: Baseline (customer-reported): $137,800/mo. Breakdown: 72% generation (GPU time), 18% embeddings (CPU & GPU), 6% storage/caching, 4% network & infra overhead. Baseline infra: mix of on-demand gpus and a small reserved pool (20% reserved), no KV prefix caching, default batching (per-request), float16 runtime. Estimated GPU-hours: 4,600 GPU-hrs/mo across A100-like instances.
redwood_optimize_proposal: Apply Redwood Optimize recommendations: 8-bit quantized runtime for 13B/7B variants, per-route adaptive batching (max latency budget 250ms), deploy prefix KV cache for top-20% retrieval flows, route non-SLA-critical routes to a 7B quantized variant with consistent truncation policy, and enable cross-request embedding caching for duplicate documents during nightly indexing.
post_optimize_estimates: Projected spend after changes: $68,400/mo (estimated). Key deltas: GPU-hours 2,200 (−52%), model unit cost per token −46% due to quantization and routing, batching savings during day reduce per-token overhead by ~15%, prefix cache reduces rerank token load by ~28% on high-reuse queries. Net monthly savings ~ $69,400 (50.3% reduction).
assumptions: Quantization to 8-bit yields 1.9x throughput improvement on target hardware with preserved output quality for non-critical routes
30% of daytime chat volume is safe to route to cheaper 7B variant with guardrails and A/B monitoring
Prefix reuse in NL workload estimated from sampling: 22% reuse on retrieval paths
No major change in request volume month-over-month; forecasts assume steady growth of 5%/quarter
key_recommendations: Enable model quantization profile Q8 on production serving for 13B and 7B variants
Create two route classes: 'slo-chat' (13B, strict latency) and 'bulk-chat' (7B quantized, higher throughput)
Configure adaptive batching by route with 40–80ms batching budget for day traffic
Provision prefix KV cache with 48GB hot tier for top retrieval routes
Implement embedding dedupe cache in nightly pipeline to avoid re-embedding unchanged docs
roi_and_payback: Estimated first-month implementation cost (SE + infra trials + QA): 18 engineer-days (~3.6 engineer-weeks) and $3,200 in trial infra. Expected first-month realized run-rate reduction to $68.4k -> monthly cash savings $69.4k. Payback on implementation effort: ~1 week after deployment (operational run-rate savings). 90-day cumulative savings > $180k net of implementation costs.
implementation_timeline: Phase 0 (2 weeks): bench quantized kernels on customer's representative snapshots and run degradation tests; Phase 1 (3 weeks): deploy route split + adaptive batching in canary (10% traffic) with telemetry; Phase 2 (1 week): enable prefix KV cache for canary flows; Phase 3 (2 weeks): full rollout and monitor evals/quality metrics. Total: ~8 weeks to full rollout with staged canaries.
risk_and_mitigation: Quality regression on routing to 7B: mitigate with A/B holdback and automatic rollback at 0.5% quality drift threshold
Unexpected token distribution spikes: mitigate with temporary autoscaling and short-term capacity overrides
Prefix cache cold-start/space: mitigate by selective warmup using last-7-day queries and LRU eviction policy
metrics_to_track_post_launch: Quality delta vs golden prompts (ROUGE/BLEU/LLM evals)
open_questions: Customer appetite for acceptable small regressions on non-core routes? (product decision)
Any compliance constraints on moving embeddings between clusters (affects embedding cache strategy)?
Will NL accept short canary periods during peak business cycle?
